title: Corporate finance I: time value of money, capital budgeting and the cost of capital
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Compute present and future values of single sums, annuities and perpetuities, value bonds and stocks, evaluate projects with NPV, IRR and payback, build project cash flows, measure risk and return, and estimate a firm's weighted average cost of capital.

weeks.1: The goal of the firm and financial statements
weeks.2: Time value of money: single sums
weeks.4: Interest rates: APR, EAR and compounding
weeks.7: Capital budgeting: NPV, IRR and payback
weeks.11: The cost of debt and WACC

blocks.deliverable: Solve ten present and future value problems.
Build a loan amortization schedule in Python.
Price three bonds and two stocks.
Week 7 midterm; build and value a project's cash flows.
Estimate a cost of equity with the CAPM.
Compute a company's WACC from public data.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Capital budgeting case: for a described expansion project, forecast incremental cash flows, estimate the company's WACC, compute NPV, IRR and payback, run sensitivity and scenario analyses in Python, and write a two-page recommendation to the board.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
